M: 嗯……但我不太确定怎么做
W: 嗯，比如说，地铁系统可以装空调
M: 啊，是的，你说得完全对

W: 听起来不错。告诉你

items.stem: How did Tariq make corn taste better?

choices.text: By slapping some butter on it.
choices.zh: 在玉米上涂一些黄油。

choices.text: By enhancing its nourishment.
choices.zh: 通过增强其营养价值。

choices.text: By growing it in South Dakota.
choices.zh: 通过在 South Dakota 种植它。

choices.text: By cooking it in vegetable oil.
choices.zh: 通过用植物油烹饪它。

items.stem: Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota?

choices.text: To introduce their corn to tourists.
choices.zh: 向游客介绍他们的玉米。

choices.text: To attend an honorary ceremony.
choices.zh: 参加一个荣誉典礼。

choices.text: To share experience with other corn growers.
choices.zh: 与其他玉米种植者分享经验。

choices.text: To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace.
choices.zh: 在该州的玉米宫展示他们的玉米。

items.stem: What did Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman do according to a news release?

choices.text: Stole mail several times.
choices.zh: 多次盗窃邮件。

choices.text: Forged postal keys illegally.
choices.zh: 非法伪造邮政钥匙。

choices.text: Attacked postmen on multiple occasions.
choices.zh: 多次袭击邮递员。

choices.text: Broke a number of postal collection boxes.
choices.zh: 破坏了多个邮政收集箱。

items.stem: What do Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman face?

choices.text: A sentence for life.
choices.zh: 终身监禁。

choices.text: Loss of all their possessions.
choices.zh: 失去所有财产。

choices.text: Twenty-three years' hard labor.
choices.zh: 二十三年苦役。

choices.text: Up to fifteen years in prison.
choices.zh: 最高十五年监禁。

items.stem: Why has the clothing industry come under attack?

choices.text: It escapes regulation and misleads consumers.
choices.zh: 它逃避监管并误导消费者。

choices.text: It ignores economically feasible recycling options.
choices.zh: 它忽视经济上可行的回收选择。

choices.text: It creates waste and severely impacts the environment.
choices.zh: 它制造废物并严重影响环境。

choices.text: It produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority.
choices.zh: 它生产的服装只有极少数人能够负担得起。

items.stem: Why did the researchers put forth such policies as production tax?

choices.text: To cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes.
choices.zh: 为了削减消费者购买优质服装的开支。

choices.text: To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable.
choices.zh: 为了使整个快时尚行业能够可持续发展。

choices.text: To incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly.
choices.zh: 为了激励制造商更加关注消费者利益。

choices.text: To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste.
choices.zh: 为了敦促制造商和消费者减少废物。

items.stem: What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry?

choices.text: Recognizing the impact on consumers.
choices.zh: 认识到对消费者的影响。

choices.text: Identifying the source of the problem.
choices.zh: 找出问题的根源。

choices.text: Abandoning the current business model.
choices.zh: 放弃当前的商业模式。

choices.text: Establishing powerful regulatory bodies.
choices.zh: 建立强有力的监管机构。

items.stem: Why is the woman complaining?

choices.text: The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.
choices.zh: 这座城市的高峰时段交通令人无法忍受。

choices.text: She cannot avoid rush-hour traffic.
choices.zh: 她无法避开高峰时段的交通。

choices.text: The local government is inefficient.
choices.zh: 当地政府效率低下。

choices.text: The city is too big to move around easily.
choices.zh: 这座城市太大了,出行不便。

items.stem: What does the woman suggest doing?

choices.text: Upgrading subway carriages.
choices.zh: 升级地铁车厢。

choices.text: Increasing the number of bus routes.
choices.zh: 增加公交线路数量。

choices.text: Air conditioning the city's subway.
choices.zh: 为城市地铁安装空调。

choices.text: Learning from other big cities.
choices.zh: 向其他大城市学习。

items.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?

choices.text: He suffers from rush-hour crowding too.
choices.zh: 他也深受高峰时段拥挤之苦。

choices.text: He is fortunate to live very near to work.
choices.zh: 他很幸运住得离工作地点非常近。

choices.text: He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.
choices.zh: 他乘坐半小时公交车上班。

choices.text: He is going to move closer to his office.
choices.zh: 他打算搬到离办公室更近的地方。

items.stem: What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation?

choices.text: Recommend to her a good house near his office.
choices.zh: 向她推荐他办公室附近的好房子。

choices.text: Send her his housing agent's telephone number.
choices.zh: 把他的房产中介的电话号码发给她。

choices.text: Tell her exactly what kind of property to look for.
choices.zh: 准确告诉她应该寻找什么类型的房产。

choices.text: Make sure the agent finds something good for her.
choices.zh: 确保中介为她找到好房子。

items.stem: What does the man say about Johnny?

choices.text: He was remembered for the scar on his cheek.
choices.zh: 他因脸颊上的疤痕而被人记住。

choices.text: He received a heart operation a few days ago.
choices.zh: 他几天前接受了心脏手术。

choices.text: He used to wear a sad face in school.
choices.zh: 他在学校时常常一副悲伤的表情。

choices.text: He had some plastic surgery done.
choices.zh: 他做了一些整形手术。

items.stem: What does the woman find puzzling?

choices.text: The man's deep sympathy for Johnny.
choices.zh: 男士对Johnny的深切同情。

choices.text: The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.
choices.zh: 男士使用"fixed"这个表达。

choices.text: The man's covering up of what happened.
choices.zh: 男士对所发生事情的掩饰。

choices.text: The man's good memory of his childhood.
choices.zh: 男士对童年时光的良好记忆。

items.stem: What did the man think of Johnny's scar?

choices.text: It gave him a noticeable smartness.
choices.zh: 它赋予了他明显的精明。

choices.text: It made him appear even more manly.
choices.zh: 它使他显得更加阳刚。

choices.text: It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.
choices.zh: 它似乎赋予了他某种独特性。

choices.text: It seemed to make up for his physical defects.
choices.zh: 它似乎弥补了他的身体缺陷。

items.stem: How could we describe the speakers' attitude towards Johnny's girlfriend?

choices.text: Liberal.
choices.zh: 宽容的。

choices.text: Hostile.
choices.zh: 敌对的。

choices.text: Indifferent.
choices.zh: 漠不关心的。

choices.text: Critical.
choices.zh: 批评的。

items.stem: How did language come into being according to researchers?

choices.text: Through deliberation.
choices.zh: 通过深思熟虑。

choices.text: Through evolution.
choices.zh: 通过进化。

choices.text: Through invention.
choices.zh: 通过发明。

choices.text: Through collaboration.
choices.zh: 通过协作。

items.stem: How did language start according to the first theory?

choices.text: With people imitating sounds around them.
choices.zh: 人们模仿周围的声音。

choices.text: With people interacting with animals close by.
choices.zh: 人们与附近的动物互动。

choices.text: With people showing each other things nearby.
choices.zh: 人们相互展示附近的事物。

choices.text: With people trying to string sounds together.
choices.zh: 人们试图将声音串联起来。

items.stem: Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory?

choices.text: Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.
choices.zh: 发出声音可以解放双手去做其他事情。

choices.text: Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages.
choices.zh: 发出声音明显比手语更容易。

choices.text: Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.
choices.zh: 发出声音使人能够更明确地表达自己的想法。

choices.text: Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see.
choices.zh: 发出声音有助于人们与看不见的人交流。

items.stem: How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?

choices.text: Well disciplined.
choices.zh: 纪律严明的

choices.text: Quite confident.
choices.zh: 相当自信的

choices.text: Somewhat selfish.
choices.zh: 有些自私的

choices.text: Highly intelligent.
choices.zh: 高度聪明的

items.stem: When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?

choices.text: When they wanted to have a competitive team member.
choices.zh: 当他们想要一个有竞争力的团队成员时

choices.text: When they were looking for a cooperative workmate.
choices.zh: 当他们在寻找一个合作的工作伙伴时

choices.text: When they found collaboration essential to them.
choices.zh: 当他们发现合作对自己至关重要时

choices.text: When they were seeking someone to help them.
choices.zh: 当他们在寻找能帮助自己的人时

items.stem: What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?

choices.text: Avoid frightening competitors.
choices.zh: 避免吓到竞争对手

choices.text: Make clear their social goal.
choices.zh: 明确自己的社交目标

choices.text: Adopt persuasive strategies.
choices.zh: 采用有说服力的策略

choices.text: Consider the consequences.
choices.zh: 考虑后果

items.stem: What can we see in the oldest cave paintings?

choices.text: Much evidence of humans capturing animals.
choices.zh: 人类捕捉动物的大量证据。

choices.text: More images of animals than humans.
choices.zh: 动物的图像多于人类的图像。

choices.text: Fewer images of buildings than animals.
choices.zh: 建筑物的图像少于动物的图像。

choices.text: Little proof of human fascination with animals.
choices.zh: 人类对动物着迷的证据很少。

items.stem: What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals?

choices.text: They were open to the public.
choices.zh: 它们向公众开放。

choices.text: They were primarily native.
choices.zh: 它们主要是本地的。

choices.text: They were kept by royalty.
choices.zh: 它们由皇室饲养。

choices.text: They were hardly injured.
choices.zh: 它们几乎没有受伤。

items.stem: What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen created the zoo?

choices.text: To enable the public to watch animals close by.
choices.zh: 使公众能够近距离观看动物。

choices.text: To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt.
choices.zh: 向埃及人介绍来自Punt的动物。

choices.text: To protect the endangered animals.
choices.zh: 保护濒危动物。

choices.text: To show off her riches and power.
choices.zh: 炫耀她的财富和权力。

items.stem: What do we learn about King Henry I's collection of animals in England?

choices.text: It was part of the royal estate.
choices.zh: 它是皇家庄园的一部分。

choices.text: It was a shelter for wild animals.
choices.zh: 它是野生动物的庇护所。

choices.text: It was the kingdom's best-equipped zoo.
choices.zh: 它是王国中设备最齐全的动物园。

choices.text: It was the first public exhibit of animals.
choices.zh: 它是第一个公开展出动物的地方。
